newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium pushes up on LME, stocks fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium pushes up on LME, stocks fall sharply.

text.p: Base metal prices were showing further gains in early Wednesday LME trading, as a positive warehouse stock report underscored the previous session's strength, traders said.
Aluminium in particular benefited from a thumping 5,225-tonne inventory drawdown, which followed stock falls of 4,700 and 2,975 tonnes on Tuesday and Monday.
Prices skipped above the $1,600 a tonne level to settle at $1,604, a $11 advance from Tuesday's kerb. Chartists now envisage a challenge of $1,625.
Traders said aluminium is being assisted to some extent by the strong copper market, although the advance is also a belated response to recent constructive fundamental developments.
Physical premiums in Europe are picking up, while fund interest is switching to the long side of the market, they added.

Copper prices were switchblading around the $2,350 a tonne level, with recent trade $3 softer at $2,345. Overnight news that the striking union at Chile's Escondida mine recommends ending the current strike, with a vote being held later on Wednesday, did inhibit the market to some extent.
However, labour talks later this week at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine and the maintenance shutdown at the Kennecott smelter in Utah remain as supportive props.
Also, nearby tightness is increasing, with the cash/threes LME backwardation at a strong $110/115 on the pre-market.
Elsewhere, nickel inventories fell by 240 tonnes, although talk still circulates of Russian cathode in Rotterdam. Prices were $20 higher at $7,445.
Zinc was $1 higher at $1,265, with stocks dropping 1,250 tonnes, while lead shed $1 to $641.
Tin was quiet, and indicated at $5,815/35, while alloy rose $23 to $1,485, helped by primary metal trends and solid physicals.
